content_html:
The story of Prophet Yunus (Jonah), peace be upon him, is the story of a noble prophet who left his people in anger, was tested by Allah with the fish, and was then saved through his tasbih (glorifying Allah) and his du'a. He returned to his people and they all believed. Here we tell it only as the Quran and authentic hadith tell it, point out the Isra'iliyyat (reports from the People of the Book) that storytellers added without evidence, and draw out practical lessons.

The Quran calls Yunus by his name and by two titles: Dhun-Nun, "the one of the fish", because "nun" is one of the Arabic words for a large fish, and Sahib al-Hut, "the companion of the fish". His name is mentioned in four surahs: An-Nisa, Al-An'am, Yunus and As-Saffat, and a whole surah, Surah Yunus, is named after him.

What is the story of Prophet Yunus in brief?

Yunus ibn Matta (Jonah son of Amittai), peace be upon him, was a prophet whom Allah sent to his people. When they did not believe, he left in anger before Allah gave him permission, and boarded a fully laden ship. Lots were drawn and he lost, and the fish swallowed him. He called out in the darkness: "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers." Allah saved him, and his people believed, so Allah gave them enjoyment of life for a time.

Its details are spread across four places: Surah As-Saffat (37:139–148), the longest; Surah Al-Anbiya (21:87–88); Surah Al-Qalam (68:48–50); and Surah Yunus (10:98). Below we put them together in the order of events.

Who was Prophet Yunus?

Yunus, peace be upon him, was one of the prophets sent as messengers. Allah says: ﴿وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ "And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers." (Surah As-Saffat 37:139, translation: Sahih International). Allah also mentioned him among the prophets He sent revelation to: ﴿إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ كَمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ مِن بَعْدِهِ ۚ وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ وَعِيسَىٰ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَارُونَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ ۚ وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ زَبُورًا﴾ "Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the book [of Psalms]." (Surah An-Nisa 4:163, translation: Sahih International). And He honoured him along with other prophets: ﴿وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَيُونُسَ وَلُوطًا ۚ وَكُلًّا فَضَّلْنَا عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ "And Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot - and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds." (Surah Al-An'am 6:86, translation: Sahih International).

His father's name, "Matta", is established in authentic hadith, as we will see in the Prophet's words ﷺ "Yunus ibn Matta". But the name of the town he was sent to is not mentioned in the Quran or in any authentic hadith from the Prophet. Books of tafsir (Quran commentary) and history made the name "Nineveh", in the land of Mosul, well known, but that comes from the People of the Book and the historians, not from the text of revelation.

Why did Prophet Yunus leave his people?

Yunus, peace be upon him, called his people to worship Allah alone and they refused, so he left them, angry with them, before the permission of his Lord to leave had come. Allah says:

﴿وَذَا النُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَاضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ أَن لَّا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ "And [mention] the man of the fish [i.e., Jonah], when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. And he called out within the darknesses, 'There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.'" (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87, translation: Sahih International)

"In anger" means angry with his people for their disbelief and their turning away, not angry with his Lord, which would not befit a prophet. As for "he thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him", the majority of mufassirun (Quran commentators) explained it as: he thought We would not put him in hardship, from the word "qadara" meaning to restrict or make tight, as in Allah's words ﴿وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ﴾ "and he whose provision is restricted" (Surah At-Talaq 65:7, translation: Sahih International). It does not mean that he thought Allah had no power over him; no believer thinks that, let alone a prophet. You will find this explanation in the tafsirs of Ibn Kathir, at-Tabari and as-Sa'di.

In Surah As-Saffat the Quran describes his leaving with a strong word: ﴿إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ﴾ "[Mention] when he ran away to the laden ship." (Surah As-Saffat 37:140, translation: Sahih International). "Abaqa" is said of a slave who runs away from his master; it is used here because he left without his Lord's permission.

What happened to Yunus on the ship?

Yunus, peace be upon him, boarded a ship full of people and goods; this is the meaning of "laden". Then Allah says:

﴿فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ الْمُدْحَضِينَ ۝ فَالْتَقَمَهُ الْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ﴾ "And he drew lots and was among the losers. Then the fish swallowed him, while he was blameworthy." (Surah As-Saffat 37:141–142, translation: Sahih International)
  • "He drew lots": he cast lots with the people on the ship; "musahamah" is drawing lots with arrows.
  • "Among the losers": he was among those who lost the draw, so it fell on him and he was thrown into the sea.
  • "Blameworthy" (mulim): he had done something for which he deserved blame, namely leaving before permission.

The Quran does not say why they drew lots. Many commentators say the ship was too heavy and about to sink; this is a well-known explanation, but it has no authentic text from the Prophet, so it is a possible explanation, not an established report.

If you want to read the commentators' explanations of these verses yourself, in Rafiq Al-Taa, Farhoon's free, ad-free app (Arabic interface) that is coming soon to Google Play, you just touch the verse in the Madinah Mushaf to open its tafsir. At-Tafsir al-Muyassar and Tafsir as-Sa'di work without internet, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir and at-Tabari are available online or after a one-time download.

Yunus in the belly of the fish: the du'a that saved him

The fish swallowed Yunus, peace be upon him, and he was in layer upon layer of darkness. He did not despair. He called on his Lord, admitting his fault and declaring his Lord free of every imperfection:

«لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ»
La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin
"There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers." (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87, translation: Sahih International)

In these three phrases he gathered the foundations of du'a: tawhid, affirming that Allah alone is God ("There is no deity except You"), tanzih, declaring Allah free of every imperfection ("exalted are You"), and admitting one's sin ("Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers"). And Allah answered him:

﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُنجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ "So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers." (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:88, translation: Sahih International)

The words ﴿وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُنجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ "And thus do We save the believers" are a general promise to every believer who calls on Allah sincerely in distress; they are not limited to Yunus, peace be upon him. The Prophet ﷺ confirmed this when he said:

"The du'a of Dhun-Nun when he called while in the belly of the fish: 'There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I have been of the wrongdoers.' No Muslim man ever calls with it for anything except that Allah answers him." Narrated by at-Tirmidhi 3505 from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him), and graded sahih by al-Albani.

Allah also made clear that his tasbih was the cause of his rescue: ﴿فَلَوْلَا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ ۝ لَلَبِثَ فِي بَطْنِهِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ "And had he not been of those who exalt Allāh, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected." (Surah As-Saffat 37:143–144, translation: Sahih International). Many commentators said this includes his tasbih in the fish and his worship before the trial, so his good deeds in ease were a cause of his rescue in hardship.

How long was Yunus in the belly of the fish?

The honest answer is: neither the Quran nor the authentic Sunnah specifies how long he stayed. The reports on this contradict each other: some say part of a day, some three days, some seven, and some forty days. These are sayings narrated from some of the early generations or taken from the People of the Book, and nothing in them is established from the Prophet ﷺ. So nothing definite can be said; the lesson is in the story, not its length.

The same applies to the many details narrated without evidence, the Isra'iliyyat (reports from the Children of Israel). The scholars' rule about them is: what agrees with the Quran and Sunnah is accepted, what contradicts them is rejected, and what revelation is silent about we neither believe nor deny, and we build no belief or ruling on it.

What happened after he came out of the fish?

Allah commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the shore in an empty land. He was weak and ill, so Allah had mercy on him and caused a plant to grow over him to give him shade:

﴿فَنَبَذْنَاهُ بِالْعَرَاءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌ ۝ وَأَنبَتْنَا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةً مِّن يَقْطِينٍ﴾ "But We threw him onto the open shore while he was ill. And We caused to grow over him a gourd vine." (Surah As-Saffat 37:145–146, translation: Sahih International)

"Al-'ara'" (the open shore) is wide land empty of trees and buildings. As for "yaqtin", most commentators said it is the gourd (dubba'), a plant with broad leaves that shades whatever is beneath it.

Surah Al-Qalam explains that this rescue was pure grace from Allah, and that without it he would have been cast onto the open land in a state of blame:

﴿فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ الْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ ۝ لَّوْلَا أَن تَدَارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَرَاءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ ۝ فَاجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ "Then be patient for the decision of your Lord, [O Muḥammad], and be not like the companion of the fish [i.e., Jonah] when he called out while he was distressed. If not that a favor [i.e., mercy] from his Lord overtook him, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was censured. And his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous." (Surah Al-Qalam 68:48–50, translation: Sahih International)

"Distressed" (makzum) means filled with grief and anguish. The address here is to the Prophet ﷺ: be patient with the harm from your people and do not be hasty as the companion of the fish was. Then the verses end with the highest of ranks: ﴿فَاجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ "And his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous." The story does not end with reproach, but with being chosen.

The people of Yunus: the only nation whose faith benefited them when they saw the punishment

Yunus, peace be upon him, returned to his people, or was sent to them, and found that they had believed:

﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَىٰ مِائَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ ۝ فَآمَنُوا فَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾ "And We sent him to [his people of] a hundred thousand or more. And they believed, so We gave them enjoyment [of life] for a time." (Surah As-Saffat 37:147–148, translation: Sahih International)

Surah Yunus explains what made this people unique among the nations:

﴿فَلَوْلَا كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَا إِيمَانُهَا إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾ "Then has there not been a [single] city that believed so its faith benefited it except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life and gave them enjoyment [i.e., provision] for a time." (Surah Yunus 10:98, translation: Sahih International)

Faith does not benefit a nation once the punishment has come down on it, as happened with Pharaoh. But when the people of Yunus saw the signs of the punishment, they believed sincerely, so Allah lifted it from them and let them enjoy life until their appointed terms. The commentators differed about when they believed relative to the fish; the verses do not specify it, so we stop at what the Quran says.

Is it allowed to say the Prophet ﷺ is better than Yunus?

In an authentic hadith, Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:

"It is not fitting for any servant to say: I am better than Yunus ibn Matta." Narrated by al-Bukhari 3416 and Muslim 2376. Al-Bukhari also narrated it from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) (3395).

Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the best of the prophets by authentic evidence, so how is the hadith understood? The best-known explanations are:

  • That he ﷺ said it out of humility.
  • That it forbids the kind of comparison that leads to belittling any of the prophets. Yunus was named in particular because someone who hears his story might think less of him, so the Prophet ﷺ closed that door.
  • That it forbids ordinary people from considering themselves better than him, so no one should say "I am better than him because I was not tested as he was".

The lesson: what happened to Yunus, peace be upon him, does not lower his rank. Allah chose him and made him one of the righteous, and we must honour him as we honour all the prophets.

Lessons from the story of Prophet Yunus

  1. Patience in calling to Allah, without haste: this is the lesson Allah directed to His Prophet ﷺ in Surah Al-Qalam.
  2. No despair with Allah: the darkness of the night, the sea and the belly of the fish all came together on Yunus, and still he was saved by du'a.
  3. Admitting your sin is the key to relief: he did not say "I was wronged"; he said "I have been of the wrongdoers". Close to this meaning is Sayyidul Istighfar, which contains "I acknowledge my sin".
  4. Know Allah in times of ease and He will know you in hardship: ﴿فَلَوْلَا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ﴾ "And had he not been of those who exalt Allāh". Frequent remembrance on ordinary days is provision for days of distress, which is why the morning and evening adhkar are a daily fortress.
  5. Sincere repentance lifts affliction: just as Allah lifted the punishment from the people of Yunus when they believed.
  6. Staying within the limits of revelation: we do not strain to know what the Quran and Sunnah are silent about, and we do not fill the story with details that have no evidence.

How to read the story of Yunus with your children

Children love the story of Yunus, and you can use it to teach them the du'a of Dhun-Nun to repeat when they are afraid or upset. Make sure you tell it to them as it comes in the Quran, without imaginary additions about the fish and what he saw in the sea, so they grow up able to tell the established from the merely reported. Read As-Saffat with them and ask: why did Allah save Yunus? Let them discover that tasbih and du'a were the reason.

For anyone who wants to go deeper into the tafsir of these verses, we compared the two best-known short tafsirs in Tafsir as-Sa'di or at-Tafsir al-Muyassar. You can read the verses of the story and their translation in Surah As-Saffat on Quran.com, and check the grading of the hadith of the du'a of Dhun-Nun in the Dorar hadith encyclopedia (Arabic).

In summary: the story of Yunus, peace be upon him, as told in the Quran, is the story of a prophet who was hasty and left before permission, was tested, glorified Allah and admitted his fault, and was saved and chosen by Allah, while his people believed and the punishment was lifted from them. Details beyond that, such as how long he stayed in the fish, are not established. The real lesson is in his du'a, which the Prophet ﷺ promised will be answered for whoever calls with it.

faq.q: What was the du'a of Yunus in the belly of the fish?
faq.a: The du'a of Yunus, peace be upon him, in the belly of the fish was: "La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin" (There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers), as in Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87. The Prophet ﷺ said that no Muslim man ever calls with it for anything except that Allah answers him. Narrated by at-Tirmidhi 3505 and graded sahih by al-Albani.

faq.q: How long did Yunus stay in the belly of the fish?
faq.a: Neither the Quran nor the authentic Sunnah specifies how long Yunus, peace be upon him, stayed in the belly of the fish. The reports contradict each other: part of a day, three days, seven, or forty. None of them is established from the Prophet ﷺ, so no specific length should be stated as certain.

Yunus, peace be upon him, is called Dhun-Nun because "nun" in Arabic is one of the names of a large fish, so Dhun-Nun means "the one of the fish", since the fish swallowed him. Allah called him by this title in Surah Al-Anbiya, and called him "the companion of the fish" in Surah Al-Qalam.

faq.q: What does "he thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him" mean?
faq.a: According to the majority of commentators, it means Yunus, peace be upon him, thought that Allah would not put him in hardship because of his leaving, from "qadara" meaning to restrict, as in "and he whose provision is restricted" (65:7). It does not mean he thought Allah had no power over him; no prophet would think that.

faq.q: In which surahs is the story of Yunus mentioned?
faq.a: The story of Yunus, peace be upon him, is told in Surah As-Saffat 37:139–148, the longest passage; in Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87–88; in Surah Al-Qalam 68:48–50; and in Surah Yunus 10:98 about his people believing. His name is also mentioned in Surahs An-Nisa and Al-An'am.

faq.q: What is the yaqtin plant that Allah caused to grow over Yunus?
faq.a: Most commentators said yaqtin is the gourd (dubba'), a plant with broad leaves that shades what is beneath it. Allah caused it to grow over Yunus, peace be upon him, as a mercy after the fish cast him onto the open shore while he was ill. Details of its fruit and how long he stayed under it have not come in any established text.
